In the 1880s Manpoondia Pillai changed it to a frame drum with a single pair of jingles and brought it onto the Carnatic stage as an accompanist to the mridangam. Its modern form is closely tied to the development of South Indian classical music. In Nepal it is called khaijadi and is used for festival dance and chant; the khanjadi bhajan of the Kathmandu Valley and the eastern hills is often performed with hymns from the Hindu Puranas.

As it is struck, the jingles in the frame add a fine jingling. Untuned it sounds high and sharp; the player can sprinkle water on the inside of the head to slacken it and get a thicker bass, though too much water deadens the sound. The tone is affected by temperature and humidity too. Pressing the rim with the fingertips of the left hand bends the pitch, and with skill you can get a glissando like the tabla's. The kanjira is a South Indian frame drum of the tambourine family. The round frame is made of jackfruit wood, one face is covered with Bengal monitor lizard skin and the other is open, and a slot in the side of the frame holds three or four small metal discs. To play it you strike the head with the right palm and fingers while the left hand holds the drum and can press the rim to change the pitch; it has no fixed tuning. It was long used in the folk and bhajan music of South Asia, and Manpoondia Pillai brought it into South Indian classical music, mainly as an accompanist to the mridangam.
演奏坎吉拉鼓時，通常以右手手掌與手指擊打鼓面，左手在側面支撐鼓框；左手指尖可靠近: You usually strike the kanjira with the palm and fingers of the right hand while the left hand supports the frame at the side; the fingertips of the left hand can press near the outer edge to bend the pitch. A beginner should work on the more complex rhythmic patterns of Indian music, and remember that the drum is not tuned to a particular pitch and sounds rather high until it is prepared. For a lower sound, sprinkle water on the inside to slacken the head, but too much water kills the tone and it needs five to ten minutes to dry; players often keep several drums to stay in condition. With practice you can produce a glissando like the tabla's.
